label: Proportional Relationships
overview: Two quantities are proportional if their ratio is constant. SAT questions involve unit rates, direct variation, and setting up proportions to find unknown values. Many real-world problems (speed, price per item, conversion between units) are proportional relationships in disguise.

conceptDiagram.caption: Direct proportion: y = kx passes through the origin; the slope k is the unit rate

workedExamples.problem: A car travels 270 miles in 4.5 hours at constant speed. At the same rate, how far does it travel in 7 hours?

commonMistakes.mistake: Setting up the proportion with mismatched units (mixing miles/hours with a different ratio)
commonMistakes.fix: Keep units consistent on each side: miles/hours = miles/hours. Label each part of the proportion.

commonMistakes.mistake: Confusing proportional (passes through origin) with linear (may not pass through origin)
commonMistakes.fix: Proportional means y/x is always constant, which requires the line to pass through (0, 0). A linear function with a non-zero y-intercept is NOT proportional.

quickTip: For proportion problems, set up the ratio with the same units in the same position on both sides, then cross-multiply and solve.
